entry.name: spell
entry.description: Accepts a numeric stream and outputs and outputs ASCII characters. Options arguments provide for forced-length messages.

arguments.name: size
arguments.description: Sets the minimum output size. Any input that doesn't "spell" to the minimum length is followed by enough fill characters (the default is the space character, 32 in ASCII) to satisfy the minimum requirement.

arguments.name: character
arguments.description: Specifies the fill character to use instead of 32. If you want to use '0' as a fill character, use any negative number as a second argument to.

messages.name: anything
messages.description: If the message begins with a symbol, all int and symbol items in the message are converted to ASCII one character at a time, and a space character (32) is placed between them. Any float items in the list are ignored. If the message begins with a float, both floats and symbols are ignored.

messages.name: int
messages.description: The ASCII value of each of the digits of the number is sent out the outlet, one digit at a time.

messages.name: list
messages.description: Each int in the list is converted to ASCII as described above, and a space character (32) is sent out between items in the list. Any float or symbol items in the list are ignored.

messages.name: symbol
messages.description: The ASCII value of each letter, digit, or other character in the symbol is sent out the outlet, one character at a time.

examples.title: Using the spell object, a modem command string or a synthesizer patch name can be translated from human terms into computer terms, and sent out the serial port in ASCII representation
